reason: The two trial slots should test lower-memory recipes with plausible paths to the quality gate. int3-g64 tests whether smaller groups recover quality over int3-g128 while keeping a 3-bit base; mixed3-4-g64 tests the same for the protected mixed recipe, which scored 0.85 at g128. Both are hypotheses: no supplied result shows either reaches 0.95 quality or throughput retention. I rank mlp3-rest4 next because it keeps most modules at 4 bits while reducing MLP expansion precision. int4-g128 remains the observed quality-safe reference at 2299.48 MiB, but another trial of it is less useful for finding a memory reduction. BF16 throughput and heldout results are absent, so no recipe is shown to pass both gates.
